findings.note: The push check no longer reads refs/remotes/*. It takes the destination's tip from 'git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<dst>' and lists commits not reachable from it; if the tip is unknown or not present locally, it lists every commit reachable from the ref, so any protected change needs signed pins. That removes the whole class (fetch, symbolic-ref, file writes, packed-refs), not only the routes I found. symbolic-ref and pack-refs are refused under R5 with its breaker on, and .git/refs/**, .git/packed-refs and .git/HEAD are protected (tamper kind): belt and braces.

findings.finding: When the remote tip cannot be read, the sequence floor for a push is 0, so a replayed older signed pins file would pass the hook; the commit-mode floor still reads refs/remotes/origin/<branch>. Both are caught by ci-check.mjs's floor, which is why CI must be required.
